newsitem.title: INDIA: India Daewoo net hit by depreciation.
newsitem.headline: India Daewoo net hit by depreciation.

text.p: Daewoo Motors India, a subsidiary of South Korea's Daewoo Corp, said on Saturday that its net profit in 1996/97 (April-March) fell sharply due to slow market growth and a rise in depreciation costs.
"We have recorded low profits because provision for depreciation has increased," Daewoo Motors managing director Shiv Awasthi said in a statement.
Daewoo Motors (India), previously called DCM Daewoo Motors Ltd, is 91.63 percent owned by South Korea's Daewoo Corp . Japan's Toyota has a minor 0.44 percent stake.
The company said on Saturday that its net profit in 1996/97 fell sharply to 10.8 million rupees ($30,167) from 496.9 million ($13.9 million) in the previous year.
The company said its depreciation costs had increased to 158.9 million rupees in 1996/97 from 74.2 million in the previous year.
Daewoo Motors' gross turnover in 1996/97 increased to 9.44 billion rupees from 5.98 billion in 1995/96. "Our expected turnover projections for 1997/98 are 16 billion rupees," Awasthi said.
Awasthi said the sales of its Cielo model car increased to 15,727 in 1996/97 from 9,044 in the previous year.
"Despite the sluggish market, the Cielo's market share in the mid-size segment is a clear indication of product acceptance," Awasthi said.
The statement said its facility to manufacture gearboxes and engines at its plant in Surajpur near Delhi had begun trial production, and would commence exports to South Korea in the current year.
Daewoo was the first to launch a mid-size car among a host of foreign car-makers that entered India under an economic reforms programme launched in 1991.
The United States' Ford, General Motors, France's Peugeot and Japan's Honda are others who have launched or are in the process of launching their products in the Indian market.

Maruti Udyog Ltd, an equal partnership joint venture between the Indian government and Japan's Suzuki Motor Corp, has been in India for more than a decade, and its model, Esteem, is also competing in the same segment.
Daewoo, which plans a total investment of $1.0 billion by 1998, said last month it also planned to launch in India during 1997/98 a small car being introduced in the world market. ($1=35.8 rupees)
